message: Need N-01: SHL returns on tangible capital

need.label: SHL returns on tangible capital
need.question: For each fiscal year from FY2018 to FY2026, what are SHL's NOPAT inputs (EBIT, amortization from IFRS 3 purchase price allocation, income tax and tax rate, income attributable to non-controlling interests) and TICAP inputs (total assets, cash, goodwill, non-interest-bearing current liabilities)?
need.rationale: ROTIC is NOPAT over average TICAP. SHL listed in March 2018, so balance sheets exist from Sep 30, 2018 and at most eight years of average TICAP (FY2019 to FY2026) can be built. That is short of the ten-year window, so the score must carry low confidence. The same SHL figures are the company side of rotic_vs_peers.

message: Need N-02: Peer returns on tangible capital

need.label: Peer returns on tangible capital
need.question: What are NOPAT and TICAP inputs for GE HealthCare and Philips over the same years, taken from their SEC XBRL filings and computed the same way as for SHL?
need.rationale: The framework compares like with like. Both peers file with the SEC, so code reads tagged audited figures with no agent. Their fiscal years end on Dec 31, three months after SHL's, and Philips reports under IFRS in euros while GE HealthCare reports under US GAAP in dollars. ROTIC is a ratio, so the currency does not matter, but the year offset has to be stated.

message: Need N-03: Revenue series by year and segment

need.label: Revenue series by year and segment
need.question: How has SHL's revenue grown each year since FY2018, in total and by segment, on a reported and a comparable basis?
need.rationale: Secular growth starts from the company's own revenue record. The segment series breaks on Oct 1, 2025: Imaging, Diagnostics, Varian and Advanced Therapies ran to the end of FY2025, and FY2026 reports Imaging, Precision Therapy and Diagnostics. Any segment trend has to say so.

message: Need N-04: End-market growth and decline risks

need.label: End-market growth and decline risks
need.question: How fast are SHL's addressable markets growing, what growth does management expect for FY2027, and does anything point to secular decline, such as diagnostics weakness in China or tariffs?
need.rationale: Secular growth scores -1 only on evidence of decline ahead. The annual report sizes the markets and names the long-term trends, the results release gives the FY2027 outlook, and outside coverage checks whether the Diagnostics problems look structural.

message: Need N-05: Debt, leases and pensions against earnings

need.label: Debt, leases and pensions against earnings
need.question: What are SHL's financial debt, lease liabilities, pension provisions, net debt and net debt to EBITDA, how much of the debt is owed to the Siemens Group, and what happens to those loans when Siemens AG deconsolidates SHL?
need.rationale: Leverage weighs debt, leases and pension obligations against earnings power. Most of SHL's debt is loans from the Siemens Group, and the FY2025 report says those loans can be terminated early once Siemens AG holds less than half the votes, so the changed shareholder structure is a leverage question.

message: Need N-06: Free cash flow against what it must fund

need.label: Free cash flow against what it must fund
need.question: What free cash flow does SHL generate, and what must it cover over the next five years: debt maturities, drawn credit facilities and dividends?
need.rationale: Liquidity scores free cash flow coverage of five-year maturities, facilities and dividends (above 2x is +1, below 1x is -1). That needs the cash flow statement, the maturity analysis, the credit facility note and the dividend proposal.

message: Need N-07: R&D spend, pipeline and forecastability

need.label: R&D spend, pipeline and forecastability
need.question: How much does SHL spend on R&D, what is the pipeline focused on, and how predictable is the business going into FY2027?
need.rationale: Research stage is about the analyst's own coverage history, which no public source can answer, so that part stays a declared gap unless the analyst supplies it. This need gives the drafter the R&D and outlook evidence for the other side of the anchor, whether the company is too hard to forecast.

message: Source S-001 (priority, rank 1): Siemens Healthineers Annual Report FY2025

source.title: Siemens Healthineers Annual Report FY2025
source.rationale: The latest audited statements and notes: income statement, balance sheet, cash flows, goodwill, intangibles, financial debt, credit facilities, maturities, segments, dividends, R&D and the subsequent-events note on the Siemens AG deconsolidation. FY2026 statements are not audited yet, so this is the base for everything the release does not cover.

message: Source S-002 (priority, rank 2): Siemens Healthineers Q4 FY2026 earnings release and financial results

source.title: Siemens Healthineers Q4 FY2026 earnings release and financial results
source.rationale: The FY2026 figures, released Nov 5, 2026: full-year income statement, balance sheet at Sep 30, 2026, cash flows, the EBITDA and purchase price allocation reconciliation by the new segments, the FY2027 outlook and the dividend proposal. BOFFIN treats a filing older than the last full fiscal year as stale, so this release is the FY2026 base until the annual report comes out on Nov 26, 2026. It is the full PDF linked from the press release, which also mentions the different shareholder structure and the Diagnostics carve-out.

message: Source S-003 (priority, rank 5): Siemens Healthineers Annual Report FY2023

source.title: Siemens Healthineers Annual Report FY2023
source.rationale: ROTIC history: income statements for FY2023 and FY2022, balance sheets at Sep 30, 2023 and 2022, and the purchase price allocation line from the segment reconciliation. The FY2025 report only goes back to Sep 30, 2024.

message: Source S-004 (priority, rank 6): Siemens Healthineers Annual Report FY2021

source.title: Siemens Healthineers Annual Report FY2021
source.rationale: ROTIC history: FY2021 and FY2020 income statements, balance sheets at Sep 30, 2021 and 2020, and the purchase price allocation line. FY2021 includes the Varian acquisition, which roughly doubled goodwill, so the ROTIC series has a step here.

message: Source S-005 (priority, rank 7): Siemens Healthineers Annual Report FY2019

source.title: Siemens Healthineers Annual Report FY2019
source.rationale: ROTIC history back to listing: FY2019 and FY2018 income statements, balance sheets at Sep 30, 2019 and 2018, and the amortization of intangibles acquired in business combinations. These years predate IFRS 16, so the lease interest add-back cannot be built the same way. Lowest relevance of the priority sources.

message: Source S-006 (tier_2, rank 1): Reuters via Euronext: Siemens Healthineers begins carve-out of diagnostics unit amid China weakness

source.title: Reuters via Euronext: Siemens Healthineers begins carve-out of diagnostics unit amid China weakness
source.rationale: Independent wire coverage of the FY2026 results, published Nov 5, 2026: slower FY2027 growth, China weakness in Diagnostics, the carve-out into Olyrian Diagnostics by mid-2028 and an analyst's view. It cross-checks the release, and any figure it gives must not contradict the tier 1 number. Fetched after every priority source.

message: Source S-007 (priority, rank 3): SEC XBRL company facts: GE HealthCare (peer)

source.title: SEC XBRL company facts: GE HealthCare (peer)
source.rationale: The closest listed peer in imaging. Audited US GAAP figures tagged by filing and period from its 10-Ks (FY2022 to FY2025, Dec year end), read by code with no agent: operating income, intangible amortization, taxes, assets, cash, goodwill, current liabilities.

message: Source S-008 (priority, rank 4): SEC XBRL company facts: Philips (peer)

source.title: SEC XBRL company facts: Philips (peer)
source.rationale: A second European health technology peer that files a 20-F with the SEC. IFRS figures in euros tagged by period (FY2020 to FY2025, Dec year end), read by code with no agent. Philips is more diversified than SHL, so it is the weaker comparison of the two.

source.rationale: An investing blog post from Aug 5, 2026 on the Q3 outlook cut and the Diagnostics weakness. Low trust: automated commentary, never the only support for a number, scanned by Guardrails before any agent reads it.

item.text: For Siemens Healthineers (SHL), using available data items, NOPAT for FY2020-FY2026 can be approximated as EBIT plus amortization from IFRS 3 purchase price allocation (only available for FY2025) less taxes at the year's effective tax rate less income attributable to non-controlling interests after tax (using the same effective tax rate). For FY2020, EBIT of €1,982 million less tax at the effective rate of 27.2% (derived from income tax of €532 million over pre-tax income of €1,954 million) less non-controlling interests of €12 million taxed at the same rate gives NOPAT of €1,433.6 million. For FY2021, EBIT of €2,573 million, effective tax rate of 27.4% (tax of €658 million over pre-tax income of €2,404 million), and non-controlling interests of €18 million, give NOPAT of €1,855.7 million. For FY2022, EBIT of €2,927 million, effective tax rate of 26.6% (tax of €746 million over pre-tax income of €2,800 million), non-controlling interests of €17 million, give NOPAT of €2,134.7 million. For FY2023, EBIT of €2,135 million, effective tax rate of 20.9% (tax of €403 million over pre-tax income of €1,928 million), non-controlling interests of €16 million, give NOPAT of €1,676.1 million. For FY2024, EBIT of €2,807 million, effective tax rate of 22.4% (tax of €564 million over pre-tax income of €2,523 million), non-controlling interests of €17 million, give NOPAT of €2,166.3 million. For FY2025, EBIT of €3,154 million plus amortization from purchase price allocation of €357 million, effective tax rate of 24.0% (tax of €686 million over pre-tax income of €2,853 million), non-controlling interests of €23 million, give NOPAT of €2,649.3 million. For FY2026, EBIT of €3,196 million, effective tax rate of 22.4% (tax of €646 million over pre-tax income of €2,890 million), non-controlling interests of €29 million, give NOPAT of €2,459.1 million. Amortization from purchase price allocation and non-interest-bearing current liabilities beyond trade payables are not available for FY2020-FY2022, FY2024 and FY2026, so NOPAT for those years omits the add-back used for FY2025.

SHL's TICAP (total assets less cash less goodwill less non-interest-bearing current liabilities, proxied here by trade payables where fuller detail is unavailable) can be computed at fiscal year-ends from FY2018 to FY2026 where data exists. At September 30, 2018, total assets of €19,758 million less cash of €519 million less goodwill of €8,176 million less trade payables of €1,278 million give TICAP of €9,785 million. At September 30, 2019, total assets of €21,429 million less cash of €920 million less goodwill of €8,590 million less trade payables of €1,403 million give TICAP of €10,516 million. At September 30, 2022, total assets of €49,056 million less cash of €1,436 million less goodwill of €19,061 million less trade payables of €2,315 million give TICAP of €26,244 million. At September 30, 2023, total assets of €46,684 million less cash of €1,642 million less goodwill of €18,118 million less a broader set of non-interest-bearing current liabilities (trade payables, contract liabilities, current provisions, current income tax liabilities and other current liabilities totaling €8,691 million) give TICAP of €18,233 million. At September 30, 2025, total assets of €44,370 million less cash of €2,175 million less goodwill of €17,124 million (no non-interest-bearing current liabilities detail available for FY2025) give TICAP of €25,071 million. At September 30, 2026, total assets of €46,707 million less cash of €2,542 million less goodwill of €17,477 million (no non-interest-bearing current liabilities detail available for FY2026) give TICAP of €26,688 million. Because the non-interest-bearing current liabilities component is inconsistent across years (trade payables only for FY2018, FY2019, FY2022; a broader set for FY2023; omitted for FY2025 and FY2026), the resulting TICAP figures and any ROTIC built on them are not strictly comparable year to year.

Combining the NOPAT estimates from c1 with year-end TICAP from c2, ROTIC can only be computed where consecutive year-end TICAP values are available one year apart: FY2023 (average of FY2022 and FY2023 TICAP). NOPAT of €1,676.1 million over an average TICAP of €22,238.5 million gives a ROTIC of 7.5% for FY2023. For FY2025 and FY2026, the prior-year TICAP (FY2024) is not computable from the data, so the year-end TICAP stands in for the average: NOPAT of €2,649.3 million over FY2025 year-end TICAP of €25,071 million gives 10.6%, and NOPAT of €2,459.1 million over FY2026 year-end TICAP of €26,688 million gives 9.2%. Averaging these three fiscal years (FY2023, FY2025, FY2026) gives a mean ROTIC of 9.1%. No TICAP is computable for FY2019-FY2021 or FY2024, so only three of the nine fiscal years from FY2018 to FY2026 could be used, well short of the ten-year window the criterion asks for.

For GE HealthCare, NOPAT for FY2022-FY2025 is computed as EBIT plus amortization of intangible assets less taxes at the year's effective rate (no equity income, non-controlling interest, or lease interest detail is available). For FY2022, EBIT of USD 2,522 million plus amortization of USD 405 million, less tax at the effective rate of 22.4% (tax of USD 563 million over pre-tax income of USD 2,512 million), gives NOPAT of USD 2,271.0 million. For FY2023, EBIT of USD 2,435 million plus amortization of USD 362 million, less tax at the effective rate of 31.5% (tax of USD 743 million over pre-tax income of USD 2,361 million), gives NOPAT of USD 1,916.8 million. For FY2024, EBIT of USD 2,625 million plus amortization of USD 312 million, less tax at the effective rate of 20.6% (tax of USD 531 million over pre-tax income of USD 2,581 million), gives NOPAT of USD 2,332.8 million. For FY2025, EBIT of USD 2,763 million plus amortization of USD 291 million, less tax at the effective rate of 22.2% (tax of USD 614 million over pre-tax income of USD 2,768 million), gives NOPAT of USD 2,376.6 million. TICAP (total assets less cash less goodwill less current liabilities net of short-term debt) is computed at each year-end: at Dec 31, 2022, total assets of USD 27,539 million less cash of USD 1,440 million less goodwill of USD 12,813 million less current liabilities net of short-term debt (current liabilities of USD 7,191 million less short-term debt of USD 15 million, or USD 7,176 million) gives TICAP of USD 6,110 million. At Dec 31, 2023, total assets of USD 32,454 million less cash of USD 2,494 million less goodwill of USD 12,936 million less current liabilities net of short-term debt (USD 8,981 million less USD 1,006 million, or USD 7,975 million) gives TICAP of USD 9,049 million. At Dec 31, 2024, total assets of USD 33,089 million less cash of USD 2,874 million less goodwill of USD 13,136 million less current liabilities net of short-term debt (USD 9,553 million less USD 1,502 million, or USD 8,051 million) gives TICAP of USD 9,028 million. At Dec 31, 2025, total assets of USD 36,906 million less cash of USD 4,492 million less goodwill of USD 13,489 million less current liabilities net of short-term debt (USD 9,105 million less USD 508 million, or USD 8,597 million) gives TICAP of USD 10,328 million. ROTIC for FY2023 (average of FY2022 and FY2023 TICAP of USD 7,579.5 million) is 25.3%. ROTIC for FY2024 (average TICAP of USD 9,038.5 million) is 25.8%. ROTIC for FY2025 (average TICAP of USD 9,678 million) is 24.6%. The mean of these three years is 25.2%.

For Philips, NOPAT for FY2021-FY2025 is computed as operating income plus amortization of intangible assets less taxes at the year's effective rate (no equity income, non-controlling interest, or lease interest detail is available). For FY2021, operating income of EUR 553 million plus amortization of EUR 568 million, less tax at the effective rate of -20.2% (tax of EUR -103 million over pre-tax income of EUR 509 million, a net tax benefit), gives NOPAT of EUR 1,347.8 million. For FY2022, operating income of EUR -1,529 million plus amortization of EUR 614 million, less tax at the effective rate of 6.5% (tax of EUR -113 million over pre-tax income of EUR -1,731 million), gives NOPAT of EUR -855.3 million. For FY2023, operating income of EUR -115 million plus amortization of EUR 556 million, less tax at the effective rate of 13.9% (tax of EUR -73 million over pre-tax income of EUR -526 million), gives NOPAT of EUR 502.2 million. For FY2024, operating income of EUR 529 million plus amortization of EUR 506 million, less tax at the effective rate of 783.0% (tax of EUR 963 million over pre-tax income of EUR 123 million), gives NOPAT of EUR -7,068.3 million, reflecting a tax expense that exceeded pre-tax income in a near break-even year. For FY2025, operating income of EUR 1,424 million plus amortization of EUR 464 million, less tax at the effective rate of 23.9% (tax of EUR 282 million over pre-tax income of EUR 1,182 million), gives NOPAT of EUR 1,437.6 million. TICAP (total assets less cash less goodwill less current liabilities net of short-term debt) is computed at each year-end: at Dec 31, 2021, total assets of EUR 30,961 million less cash of EUR 2,303 million less goodwill of EUR 10,637 million less current liabilities net of short-term debt (EUR 7,450 million less EUR 506 million, or EUR 6,944 million) gives TICAP of EUR 11,077 million. At Dec 31, 2022, total assets of EUR 30,688 million less cash of EUR 1,172 million less goodwill of EUR 10,238 million less current liabilities net of short-term debt (EUR 7,934 million less EUR 931 million, or EUR 7,003 million) gives TICAP of EUR 12,275 million. At Dec 31, 2023, total assets of EUR 29,406 million less cash of EUR 1,869 million less goodwill of EUR 9,876 million less current liabilities net of short-term debt (EUR 8,287 million less EUR 654 million, or EUR 7,633 million) gives TICAP of EUR 10,028 million. At Dec 31, 2024, total assets of EUR 28,976 million less cash of EUR 2,401 million less goodwill of EUR 10,383 million less current liabilities net of short-term debt (EUR 8,146 million less EUR 526 million, or EUR 7,620 million) gives TICAP of EUR 8,572 million. At Dec 31, 2025, total assets of EUR 26,944 million less cash of EUR 2,794 million less goodwill of EUR 9,271 million less current liabilities net of short-term debt (EUR 7,509 million less EUR 1,151 million, or EUR 6,358 million) gives TICAP of EUR 8,521 million. ROTIC for FY2022 (average of FY2021 and FY2022 TICAP of EUR 11,676 million) is -7.3%. ROTIC for FY2023 (average TICAP of EUR 11,151.5 million) is 4.5%. ROTIC for FY2024 (average TICAP of EUR 9,300 million) is -76.0%, reflecting the FY2024 NOPAT distortion from the unusually high effective tax rate. ROTIC for FY2025 (average TICAP of EUR 8,546.5 million) is 16.8%. The mean of these four years is -15.5%.

Reported revenue grew in most years from €13,429 million in FY2018 to €23,630 million in FY2026, a cumulative increase of 76.0% over the eight-year span, with comparable growth of 5.9% in FY2025 and 4.0% in FY2026.

Management guides comparable revenue growth of between 4.0% and 5.0% for fiscal year 2027 versus fiscal year 2026, a range that excludes any change in the level of tariffs, which is flagged as a potential risk to the business.

Addressable markets sized in fiscal year 2025 were slightly more than €31 billion for Imaging, approximately €37 billion for Diagnostics, more than €6 billion for Varian and over €7 billion for Advanced Therapies; markets grew moderately for Imaging, slightly for Diagnostics, and strongly for Varian and Advanced Therapies in fiscal year 2025. Diagnostics market growth was dampened by temporary weakness in China, the world's largest Diagnostics market, and Diagnostics comparable revenue declined 4.2% in Q4 fiscal year 2026, with prolonged China weakness identified as a potential structural challenge to the investment narrative.

Demographic and access trends support demand: the number of over-60s is projected to more than double by 2050, and access to medical care remains insufficient for over half of the world population. In China, healthcare reform continues via the 14th Five Year Plan with volume-based and centralized public procurement, flat-rate reimbursement and health-service charging reforms, localization of government procurement, and an anti-corruption campaign active since summer 2023 that has become a new normal, all cited as factors affecting market development.

At September 30, 2025, SHL's total financial debt was €14,793 million, made up of €268 million short-term financial debt and current maturities, and €487 million long-term financial debt, which together give a combined short- and long-term financial debt of €755 million; the remainder is owed to the Siemens Group, whose current and non-current financing liabilities were €3,183 million and €10,855 million, summing to €14,038 million of Siemens Group financing liabilities, which together with the €755 million reconciles to €14,793 million total financial debt. Current and non-current lease liabilities were €176 million and €487 million, of which €11 million and €18 million respectively are owed to the Siemens Group, for total lease liabilities of €663 million. Pension provisions were €488 million. Net debt was €11,985 million and net debt including pensions was €12,472 million. EBITDA was €4,450 million, and net debt including pensions to EBITDA was reported at 2.8x. Interest expenses from financing arrangements with the Siemens Group were €335 million in fiscal year 2025.

At September 30, 2026, short-term financial debt and current maturities of long-term financial debt were €277 million and long-term financial debt was €589 million, together €866 million of short- and long-term financial debt, up from the combined €755 million a year earlier. Pension provisions fell to €333 million from €488 million. Current liabilities to the Siemens Group were €2,932 million and non-current liabilities to the Siemens Group were €10,943 million, together €13,875 million of Siemens Group liabilities.

In fiscal year 2025, two loans from the Siemens Group totaling €1.2 billion were settled. As of September 30, 2025, total current and non-current liabilities to the Siemens Group from loans were €1,919 million and €10,837 million, together €12,756 million, covering US dollar-denominated loans maturing between fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2046 (carrying amounts of €1,484 million, €1,438 million, €1,059 million, €1,482 million, €1,266 million and €843 million) and euro-denominated loans maturing between fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2032 (carrying amounts of €300 million, €500 million, €850 million, €600 million, €700 million, €500 million, €700 million and €750 million), plus other loans of €135 million current and €149 million non-current. The actual volume-weighted average interest rate on the US dollar-denominated loans was approximately 0.5% as of September 30, 2025. Various agreements between Siemens Healthineers AG and the Siemens Group provide for early termination rights for Siemens AG or affiliated companies if Siemens AG's shares or voting rights fall below 50% plus one share, with market value compensation clauses on some loans; loans whose market value at September 30, 2025 was according to preliminary estimates significantly below book value include a compensation clause, with a currently estimated one-off positive effect that may be offset by correspondingly higher financing expenses in subsequent periods due to currently higher market interest rates.

Non-derivative financial liabilities due in fiscal years 2026 and 2027 and 2028-2030 total €13,499 million. Siemens Healthineers also had €2.5 billion and €2.0 billion multicurrency revolving credit facilities available as of September 30, 2025, of which €451 million was drawn. The fiscal 2025 proposed dividend per share of €1.00 implies total dividend payments of about €1,117 million; approximating five years of such dividends at this per-share rate gives €5,585 million. Adding the five-year maturities, the facilities drawn amount, and five years of dividends gives a total funding need of €19,535 million. Free cash flow was €2,714 million in fiscal year 2025 and about €2,446 million in fiscal year 2026; using the FY2026 figure as a run rate, five years of free cash flow would total about €12,230 million, which is 0.6 times the five-year funding need. Using the FY2025 free cash flow figure as the run rate, five years would total €13,570 million, which is 0.7 times the five-year funding need.

In fiscal year 2025, cash flows from operating activities were €3,532 million and additions to intangible assets and property, plant and equipment were €818 million, together implying free cash flow of €2,714 million, matching the reported free cash flow figure. Dividends paid to shareholders in fiscal year 2025 were €1,066 million and repayment of long-term debt was €188 million; together these cash outflows were €1,254 million, which free cash flow of €2,714 million covered 2.2 times.

R&D expenses rose from €1,918 million in FY2024 to €1,958 million in FY2025 to €1,969 million in FY2026, a rise of €51 million over the two years. In FY2025 R&D intensity was 8% of revenue, supported by more than 13,000 R&D employees, more than 25,000 technical intellectual property rights and more than 16,000 granted patents as of September 30, 2025.

SHL's ROTIC could be computed for only three of the ten fiscal years asked for (FY2023, FY2025, FY2026), using a proxy that omits full non-interest-bearing current liabilities detail in most years and substitutes year-end TICAP for the average in two years. The mean of these three years is 9.1%, below the 15% bar for a plus-one score and essentially at the 10% bar for a minus-one score. Confidence is low given the short series and inconsistent TICAP methodology across years.

Over the years each company's data allows, SHL's mean ROTIC across FY2023, FY2025 and FY2026 is 9.1%, below GE HealthCare's mean ROTIC across FY2023-FY2025 of 25.2%. Philips' mean ROTIC across FY2022-FY2025 is -15.5%, which is lower than SHL's, but that figure is distorted by a FY2024 tax expense exceeding pre-tax income and by a loss year in FY2022, so it is not a reliable upper comparator. Against GE HealthCare, the higher of the two peer figures and the one less affected by one-off items, SHL's computed ROTIC is lower.

Revenue has grown cumulatively 76.0% from FY2018 to FY2026 (c1), and management guides comparable growth for FY2027 starting at 4.0% (c2), supported by demographic tailwinds such as a doubling of the over-60 population by 2050 and insufficient access to care for over half the world's population (c4). However, the Diagnostics segment, sized at approximately €37 billion in FY2025 (c3), has shown weakness tied to China healthcare reforms, with Diagnostics comparable revenue declining 4.2% in Q4 FY2026 and prolonged China weakness flagged as a potential structural challenge (c3). Tariffs are also excluded from the FY2027 outlook as an unquantified risk (c2). This mix of continued overall growth alongside a segment-level headwind that may be structural falls short of unambiguous secular decline but is not a clean secular growth story either, so a neutral score is warranted.

Net debt including pensions to EBITDA was 2.8x in FY2025 (D-216), with most financial debt owed to the Siemens Group (€14,038 million of €14,793 million total financial debt in FY2025, per c1's computations), and loans owed to the Siemens Group (€12,756 million per c3) carry early-termination rights for Siemens AG if its voting rights in SHL fall below 50% plus one share (D-107), with compensation clauses on loans whose market value is significantly below book value that could raise financing expenses in subsequent periods (D-110). Short- and long-term financial debt outside the Siemens Group rose from €755 million (c1) to €866 million (c2) between FY2025 and FY2026, while pension provisions fell from €488 million to €333 million (D-140, D-197) and Siemens Group liabilities fell slightly from €14,038 million to €13,875 million (c1, c2).

Free cash flow of about €2,446 million in fiscal year 2026 (c1) or €2,714 million in fiscal year 2025 (c1), projected over five years, covers only 0.6 to 0.7 times the combined five-year non-derivative financial-liability maturities of €13,499 million, the €451 million drawn on revolving credit facilities, and five years of dividends at the €1.00 per share rate (c1), both below the 1x threshold for a -1 score. On a narrower basis covering only fiscal 2025 dividends paid and long-term debt repayment, free cash flow covered these by 2.2 times (c2), but the broader five-year maturity and facility test falls below 1x.

item.text: For Philips, NOPAT for FY2021-FY2025 is computed as operating income plus amortization of intangible assets less taxes at the year's effective rate (no equity income, non-controlling interest, or lease interest detail is available). For FY2021, operating income of EUR 553 million plus amortization of EUR 568 million, less tax at the effective rate of -20.2% (tax of EUR -103 million over pre-tax income of EUR 509 million, a net tax benefit), gives NOPAT of EUR 1,347.8 million. For FY2022, operating income of EUR -1,529 million plus amortization of EUR 614 million, less tax at the effective rate of 6.5% (tax of EUR -113 million over pre-tax income of EUR -1,731 million), gives NOPAT of EUR -855.3 million. For FY2023, operating income of EUR -115 million plus amortization of EUR 556 million, less tax at the effective rate of 13.9% (tax of EUR -73 million over pre-tax income of EUR -526 million), gives NOPAT of EUR 502.2 million. For FY2024, operating income of EUR 529 million plus amortization of EUR 506 million, less tax at the effective rate of 782.9% (tax of EUR 963 million over pre-tax income of EUR 123 million), gives NOPAT of EUR -7,068.3 million, reflecting a tax expense that exceeded pre-tax income in a near break-even year. For FY2025, operating income of EUR 1,424 million plus amortization of EUR 464 million, less tax at the effective rate of 23.9% (tax of EUR 282 million over pre-tax income of EUR 1,182 million), gives NOPAT of EUR 1,437.6 million. TICAP (total assets less cash less goodwill less current liabilities net of short-term debt) is computed at each year-end: at Dec 31, 2021, total assets of EUR 30,961 million less cash of EUR 2,303 million less goodwill of EUR 10,637 million less current liabilities net of short-term debt (EUR 7,450 million less EUR 506 million, or EUR 6,944 million) gives TICAP of EUR 11,077 million. At Dec 31, 2022, total assets of EUR 30,688 million less cash of EUR 1,172 million less goodwill of EUR 10,238 million less current liabilities net of short-term debt (EUR 7,934 million less EUR 931 million, or EUR 7,003 million) gives TICAP of EUR 12,275 million. At Dec 31, 2023, total assets of EUR 29,406 million less cash of EUR 1,869 million less goodwill of EUR 9,876 million less current liabilities net of short-term debt (EUR 8,287 million less EUR 654 million, or EUR 7,633 million) gives TICAP of EUR 10,028 million. At Dec 31, 2024, total assets of EUR 28,976 million less cash of EUR 2,401 million less goodwill of EUR 10,383 million less current liabilities net of short-term debt (EUR 8,146 million less EUR 526 million, or EUR 7,620 million) gives TICAP of EUR 8,572 million. At Dec 31, 2025, total assets of EUR 26,944 million less cash of EUR 2,794 million less goodwill of EUR 9,271 million less current liabilities net of short-term debt (EUR 7,509 million less EUR 1,151 million, or EUR 6,358 million) gives TICAP of EUR 8,521 million. ROTIC for FY2022 (average of FY2021 and FY2022 TICAP of EUR 11,676 million) is -7.3%. ROTIC for FY2023 (average TICAP of EUR 11,151.5 million) is 4.5%. ROTIC for FY2024 (average TICAP of EUR 9,300 million) is -76.0%, reflecting the FY2024 NOPAT distortion from the unusually high effective tax rate. ROTIC for FY2025 (average TICAP of EUR 8,546.5 million) is 16.8%. The mean of these four years is -15.5%.

item.text: In fiscal year 2025, two loans from the Siemens Group totaling €1.2 billion were settled. As of September 30, 2025, total current and non-current liabilities to the Siemens Group from loans were €1,919 million and €10,837 million, together €12,756 million, including US dollar-denominated loans maturing in fiscal 2026, 2027, 2028, 2031, 2041 and 2046 (carrying amounts of €1,484 million, €1,438 million, €1,059 million, €1,482 million, €1,266 million and €843 million) and euro-denominated loans maturing in fiscal 2026, 2028, 2029, 2030 and 2032 (carrying amounts of €300 million, €500 million, €850 million, €600 million, €700 million, €500 million, €700 million and €750 million), plus other loans of €135 million current and €149 million non-current. The actual volume-weighted average interest rate on the US dollar-denominated loans was approximately 0.5% as of September 30, 2025. Various agreements between Siemens Healthineers AG and the Siemens Group provide for early termination rights for Siemens AG or affiliated companies if Siemens AG's shares or voting rights fall below 50% plus one share, with market value compensation clauses on some loans; all loans whose market value at September 30, 2025 was according to preliminary estimates significantly below book value include this compensation clause, with a currently estimated one-off positive effect that may be offset by correspondingly higher financing expenses in subsequent periods due to currently higher market interest rates.

item.text: Revenue has grown cumulatively 76.0% from FY2018 to FY2026 (c1), and management guides comparable growth for FY2027 starting at 4.0% (c2), supported by demographic tailwinds such as a doubling of the over-60 population by 2050 and insufficient access to care for over half the world's population (c4). However, the Diagnostics segment, sized at approximately €37 billion in FY2025 (c3), has shown weakness tied to China healthcare reforms, with Diagnostics comparable revenue declining 4.2% in Q4 FY2026 and prolonged China weakness flagged as a potential structural challenge (c3). Tariffs are also excluded from the FY2027 outlook as an unquantified risk (c2). This mix of continued overall growth alongside a segment-level headwind that may be structural falls short of unambiguous secular decline but is not a clean secular growth story either, so a neutral score is warranted.
